goals: Compute mean, median, mode, variance and standard deviation
Choose the right "typical value" for skewed data
Use quartiles and the IQR to describe spread
why: Every report starts with descriptive statistics. Choosing mean vs median wrongly is how "average salary" headlines mislead whole countries.
explain: **Centre**: the **mean** is the arithmetic average; the **median** is the middle value when sorted; the **mode** is the most frequent value.
The mean is pulled by extreme values; the median is not. For skewed data (salaries, house prices, delivery times) the median is usually the honest "typical" value.

**Spread**: the **standard deviation** (SD) is the typical distance from the mean. The **interquartile range** (IQR = Q3 − Q1) is the width of the middle 50% and, like the median, is robust to outliers.
Always report a centre **and** a spread. "Average delivery 2 days" means something very different with an SD of 0.2 days than with an SD of 3 days.

formula.plain: Mean = sum ÷ count. Sample SD = square root of the average squared distance from the mean (dividing by n − 1 for a sample).

example.title: Five employees' monthly bonus (₹ thousand)
example.result: Saying "the average bonus is ₹22,400" is technically true and completely misleading. The median of ₹3,000 describes a typical employee.

mistakes: Using the mean for heavily skewed data.
Reporting a centre without any measure of spread.
Dividing by n instead of n − 1 for a sample SD (a small difference for large n).
takeaways: Mean is sensitive to outliers; median is robust
IQR and box plots summarise skewed data well
use: First step of every analysis and dashboard
Data quality checks (impossible minimums and maximums)

practice.code:
import pandas as pd
s = pd.Series([2, 3, 3, 4, 100])
print(s.describe())                 # count, mean, std, min, quartiles, max
print("median", s.median(), "IQR", s.quantile(.75) - s.quantile(.25))

check.q: House prices in a city are right-skewed. Which "typical price" is best?
check.why: The median ignores the few very expensive houses.
